dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Matrix-vector multiplication: for a matrix A and vector x, the resulting vector has component (Ax)_i = sum over all j in Fin n of A_ij x_j.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical norm on the finite product of real coordinate spaces, namely the supremum norm: max_i |x_i| when n is positive, and 0 for the empty product.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the left-hand side of the concluding inequality, so that inequality is ‖δ‖∞ ≤ ‖δ‖₂.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The conjunction that the transpose of Q is both a left and a right inverse of Q: QᵀQ = I and QQᵀ = I.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Entrywise scalar multiplication of a matrix: (sA)_ij = s A_ij.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Euclidean norm of a real vector: sqrt(sum_i x_i²).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, possibly zero.
Q is an arbitrary real n-by-n matrix, represented as a function Fin n → Fin n → Real.
e is an arbitrary real vector of length n, represented as a function Fin n → Real.
s is an arbitrary real scalar.
δ is an existentially quantified real vector of length n whose three required properties are mutually dependent on the same witness.
hypotheses: QᵀQ=I: for every i,j in Fin n, sum_k Q_ki Q_kj equals 1 if i=j and 0 otherwise.
QQᵀ=I: for every i,j in Fin n, sum_k Q_ik Q_jk equals 1 if i=j and 0 otherwise.
conclusions: There exists a vector δ such that (sQ)δ=e; componentwise, for every i, sum_j (s Q_ij)δ_j=e_i.
The Euclidean norm of that same δ satisfies the exact equality sqrt(sum_i δ_i²)=sqrt(sum_i e_i²)/s.
The same δ satisfies max_i |δ_i|≤sqrt(sum_i δ_i²), with the finite-product norm interpreted as 0 when n=0.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the coordinate set {0,…,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.
(Ax)_i := sum over j in Fin n of A_ij x_j.
‖x‖∞ := max_i |x_i| for nonempty Fin n, with the finite-function norm equal to 0 for Fin 0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension n, every real n-by-n matrix Q, every real vector e, and every positive real scalar s, if the transpose of Q is both a left and a right inverse of Q, then there exists a real vector δ such that multiplying δ by the scaled matrix sQ gives e exactly, the Euclidean norm of δ is exactly the Euclidean norm of e divided by s, and the supremum norm of δ is at most its Euclidean norm.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n is not required to be positive. When n=0, all indexwise inverse conditions and vector equalities are vacuous, the unique vectors are empty, both norms are 0, and the conclusion is trivial.
The matrix is square and is assumed to satisfy both QᵀQ=I and QQᵀ=I exactly.
The scalar s must be strictly positive; zero and negative scales are excluded.
There is no restriction on e.
The proposition uses exact real arithmetic, exact matrix equations, and exact norm equality; it encodes no approximation, perturbation, rounding, tolerance, or error bound.
The conclusion is existential and does not explicitly state a formula or uniqueness for δ, although the hypotheses imply that the solution is unique and can be derived as δ=Qᵀe/s.
The square root is applied only to sums of real squares, which are nonnegative.
